title: Mole Calculations
description: Avogadro constant, n = m/Mr, n = c × V, and reacting masses from balanced equations.

method_card.title: Mole Calculations
method_card.content:
The mole is the chemist's counting unit. One mole always contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (the Avogadro constant). Because atoms and molecules are too small to count directly, we weigh them instead.

Core equations — learn all three:

  • \(n = \dfrac{m}{M_r}\) — moles from mass and relative formula mass
  • \(n = c \times V\) — moles from concentration (mol/dm³) and volume (dm³)
  • \(M_r = \dfrac{m}{n}\) and \(m = n \times M_r\) — rearrangements of the first equation

Finding Mᵣ step by step: Write the formula, count each type of atom, multiply by the Aᵣ from the data sheet, add up. For Ca(OH)₂: 1×40 + 2×(16+1) = 74.

Reacting masses — five-step routine:

  1. Write (or check) the balanced equation
  2. Read the molar ratio from the coefficients
  3. Calculate moles of the known substance: n = m ÷ Mᵣ
  4. Scale using the ratio to get moles of the unknown
  5. Convert back to mass: m = n × Mᵣ

Volume unit rule: n = c × V only works when V is in dm³. Divide cm³ by 1000 first.
steps: Calculate Mᵣ by adding all Aᵣ values in the formula
Find moles: n = m ÷ Mᵣ (or n = c × V if given concentration and volume)
For reacting masses: apply the molar ratio from the balanced equation
Convert moles back to mass: m = n × Mᵣ
Check using conservation of mass: total reactant mass = total product mass

exam_context.frequency: Very high — mole calculations underpin almost every quantitative chemistry question

worked_examples.question: Calculate the number of moles in 22 g of carbon dioxide, CO₂. (Aᵣ: C = 12, O = 16)
Calculate the mass of MgO produced when 12 g of magnesium burns in oxygen. Balanced equation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. (Aᵣ: Mg = 24, O = 16)

steps.label: Step 3 — Find Mᵣ of MgO and mass

worked_examples.question: 0.010 mol of Na₂CO₃ is dissolved in water to make 250 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm³.

bronze.display: Calculate the Mᵣ of water, H₂O. (Aᵣ: H = 1, O = 16)
bronze.equation_hint: Add up all Aᵣ values in the formula.

misconceptions.message: H₂O has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom. Mᵣ = (2×1) + 16 = 18.

bronze.display: How many moles are in 44 g of CO₂? (Aᵣ: C = 12, O = 16)
Calculate the number of moles in 9.0 g of water, H₂O. (Mᵣ = 18)

misconceptions.message: Divide mass by Mᵣ, not multiply. n = 9.0 ÷ 18 = 0.50 mol.

bronze.display: What mass does 2.0 mol of NaOH represent? (Aᵣ: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
The Avogadro constant is 6.02 × 10²³. How many molecules are in 0.5 mol of water?
bronze.equation_hint: Multiply moles by the Avogadro constant.

bronze.display: Calculate the Mᵣ of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄. (Aᵣ: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)
bronze.equation_hint: Count each atom type: 2 H, 1 S, 4 O.

bronze.display: Calculate the mass of 0.25 mol of CuSO₄. (Aᵣ: Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16)
How many moles are in 5.85 g of NaCl? (Aᵣ: Na = 23, Cl = 35.5)

silver.display: 16 g of copper oxide (CuO) reacts with hydrogen: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. Calculate the mass of copper produced. (Aᵣ: Cu = 64, O = 16)
silver.equation_hint: n = m ÷ Mᵣ, apply 1:1 mole ratio, then m = n × Aᵣ(Cu).

misconceptions.message: The ratio from the equation is 1:1, so moles of Cu = moles of CuO.

silver.display: 10.0 g of calcium carbonate decomposes: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of CO₂ produced. (Mᵣ: CaCO₃ = 100, CO₂ = 44)
silver.equation_hint: n = m ÷ Mᵣ(CaCO₃), apply 1:1 ratio, m = n × Mᵣ(CO₂).

silver.display: Calculate the number of moles in 200 cm³ of a 0.50 mol/dm³ solution.
silver.equation_hint: Convert cm³ to dm³ first, then n = c × V.

misconceptions.message: 200 cm³ = 0.20 dm³. n = 0.50 × 0.20 = 0.10 mol. Don’t use 200 directly.

silver.display: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Calculate the mass of NaOH formed when 4.6 g of sodium reacts completely. (Aᵣ: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
What mass of magnesium reacts completely with 8 g of sulfur? Mg + S → MgS. (Aᵣ: Mg = 24, S = 32)
silver.equation_hint: 1:1 mole ratio. Find moles of S, then mass of Mg.

silver.display: 4.0 g of NaOH is dissolved in water to make 500 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm³. (Mᵣ = 40)
silver.equation_hint: n = m ÷ Mᵣ, then c = n ÷ V (V in dm³).

gold.display: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Calculate the mass of iron produced from 24 g of iron(III) oxide. (Mᵣ: Fe₂O₃ = 160, Aᵣ: Fe = 56)

misconceptions.message: One mole of Fe₂O₃ produces two moles of Fe. Double the moles.

gold.display: 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃. What mass of AlCl₃ is produced from 5.4 g of aluminium? (Aᵣ: Al = 27, Cl = 35.5)

misconceptions.message: The ratio 2Al : 2AlCl₃ simplifies to 1:1, so moles of Al = moles of AlCl₃.

gold.display: A student dissolves 5.3 g of Na₂CO₃ to make 250 cm³ of solution. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm³. (Aᵣ: Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: 250 cm³ = 0.25 dm³. Divide by 1000 before using c = n ÷ V.

gold.display: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. What mass of ammonia forms from 28 g of nitrogen gas? (Aᵣ: N = 14, H = 1)

misconceptions.message: From the equation, 1 mol N₂ produces 2 mol NH₃. Double the moles of N₂.

gold.display: A student identifies an unknown gas: 5.6 g of the gas contains 0.25 mol. What is the Mᵣ of the gas? Name the gas if it is a diatomic element with Aᵣ = 14.

misconceptions.message: Mᵣ = mass ÷ moles = 5.6 ÷ 0.25 = 22.4. This is close to the Aᵣ of nitrogen (14), but that’s for N, not N₂ (Mr = 28). Accept Mᵣ = 22.4.
Rearrange n = m ÷ Mᵣ to get Mᵣ = m ÷ n = 5.6 ÷ 0.25 = 22.4.

gold.display: 25.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ HCl reacts with excess zinc: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Calculate the mass of zinc that reacts. (Aᵣ: Zn = 65)

misconceptions.message: 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³. Divide by 1000 before using n = c × V.

knowledge_checks.q: How many particles are there in one mole of any substance?
What is the Mᵣ of CO₂? (Aᵣ: C = 12, O = 16)
The number of moles is calculated by dividing the mass by the _____ formula mass.
In a balanced equation, the numbers in front of each formula give the _____ ratios.
Match each term to its definition.
right: Sum of relative atomic masses of all atoms in one formula unit
Mass of one atom relative to one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom

flashcard_questions.a: 6.02 × 10²³ per mole — the number of particles in one mole of any substance.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the equation linking moles, mass and relative formula mass?
How do you find the number of moles from concentration and volume?
flashcard_questions.a: n = c × V, where V must be in dm³ (divide cm³ by 1000).

flashcard_questions.q: What is the Mᵣ of NaOH? (Aᵣ: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
How many moles are in 22 g of CO₂? (Mᵣ = 44)
What are the five steps for a reacting-masses calculation?
flashcard_questions.a: 1) Balanced equation; 2) molar ratio; 3) moles of known substance; 4) moles of unknown via ratio; 5) mass = moles × Mᵣ.

flashcard_questions.q: In the equation 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, what is the Mg : MgO mole ratio?
flashcard_questions.a: 1:1 — two moles of Mg produce two moles of MgO.

flashcard_questions.q: What does conservation of mass tell you about reacting masses?
flashcard_questions.a: Total mass of reactants = total mass of products — atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.

glossary_terms.definition: The amount of substance that contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles; one mole of any element has a mass in grams equal to its relative atomic mass.
The number of particles in one mole of any substance, equal to 6.02 × 10²³ per mole.
The mass of an atom relative to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom; found on the periodic table for each element.
The sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in one formula unit of a compound.
In a chemical reaction, the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products; atoms are rearranged but not created or destroyed.
